subject: Workplace Skills
title: Choosing Your Battles
description: A fast breakdown of Choosing Your Battles for builders.

hook.text: He fought every minor policy change. Within a year, leadership stopped listening to his valid concerns too.

buildup.text: Political capital is finite. Spending it on small issues leaves nothing for the battles that truly matter.

discovery.text: Before engaging, ask: Does this affect outcomes I care about? Can I actually influence the result?

twist.text: Letting small things go isn't weakness. It's strategic patience that preserves leverage for big moments.

climax.text: Save your strongest pushback for decisions that are hard to reverse and have lasting impact.

punchline.text: Spend capital wisely. Fight only what matters most.

quiz.question: Why should you be selective about workplace battles?
options: Political capital is finite and overuse makes people stop listening
Managers prefer employees who never disagree
